blocks.content: The United Nations & the Unimplemented Plebiscite

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: UN Security Council Resolution 47 (1948) outlined a three-step process: Pakistani withdrawal, Indian troop reduction, and a plebiscite under UN supervision.
India maintains that the plebiscite was never held because Pakistan failed to fulfill the mandatory first step of complete military withdrawal from the region.
The 1972 Simla Agreement converted the 1971 ceasefire line into the Line of Control (LoC) and committed both nations to bilateral dispute resolution.
Through the 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement, Pakistan illegally ceded the Shaksgam Valley (5,180 sq km) in PoK to China.

China officially treats Kashmir as a bilateral historical dispute between India and Pakistan, while actively constructing the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) through Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir.

blocks.content: The 1972 Simla Agreement fundamentally altered the diplomatic framework of Jammu and Kashmir by establishing that all disputes between India and Pakistan must be resolved strictly through bilateral negotiations, excluding third-party intervention.

rows: Multilateral mechanism involving UN mediation and supervision
Strictly bilateral framework between India and Pakistan
Complete withdrawal of Pakistani forces and irregulars from J&K
Mutual commitment to respect the Line of Control without altering it unilaterally
Envisaged international plebiscite administrator and commission
Explicitly excludes all external third-party mediation or international arbitration

items: UNSC Resolution 47 explicitly mandated Pakistan's complete withdrawal of forces from J&K as the primary prerequisite before any plebiscite could be considered.
The 1972 Simla Agreement superseded the UN framework by establishing a strict bilateral framework and converting the Ceasefire Line into the Line of Control (LoC).
The 1963 Sino-Pakistan Boundary Agreement involved the illegal ceding of Shaksgam Valley to China, which India maintains is an integral part of Indian territory.
